newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent wipes out gains in volatile expiry marke.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent wipes out gains in volatile expiry marke.

text.p: IPE Brent wiped out Wednesday's gains in early trade on Thursday as confidence inspired by the stronger close dwindled.
March Brent was trading 46 cents off at $23.19 a barrel at 1105 GMT. Traders had viewed Wednesday's higher close -- the first in five sessions -- as a relatively positive sign.
"Obviously it wasn't enough," said one trader. "People are selling into the rallies. There's plenty of paper on offer out there."
Traders said the market would fairly volatile due to the expiry of the Feb contract at the end of Thursday's session.
The Feb contract was trading 28 cents off at $23.56. "It's in a world of it's own but it will shake up the market a bit today."
Gas oil, meanwhile, was stronger as it played catch-up with Brent's gain which were made after the complex had closed.
The February contract was trading $2.25 higher at $215.75 a tonne.
Traders said gas oil was also being supported by forecasts for cold weather in the world's key heating oil market of the northeast United States.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said the coldest air mass of the season was due to arrive in the northeast United States late on Friday and last until Monday.
